Author: Prabhat Kumar Singh
Bench: Prabhat Kumar Singh
 In The High Court Of Judicature At Patna
 Criminal Miscellaneous No.43838 of 2023
 Arising Out of Ps. Case No.-163 Year-2013 Thana- Dehri Town Distric

 Sone, Rohtas, Bihar
 2. Ambika Singh @ Ambika Prasad Singh Son Of Late
 Mundar Singh Resident Of Bose Bagan, Lal Bangla,
 Dehri-On-Sone, Dalmianagar, Rohtas, Bihar. 821305
 3. Lalan Paswan Son Of Suba Paswan Resident Of Village-
 Kachar, Ps- Kachar, Dist- Gaya, Bihar- 824206

 1 . The State Of Bihar
 2. Santosh Kumar S/O Suryadeo Yadav R/O New Area, Joda 
 Mandir, P.S - Dehri On Sone, Distt. - Rohtas, Bihar 
 ... ... Opposite Party/S

 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr.Avanish Kumar Singh, Advocate
 For the Opposite Party/s : Mr. Md. Shakir Ahmad , App

 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Prabhat Kumar Singh
 Oral Order 
4 01-04-2024 Heard learned counsel for the parties. 
Ruchi Singh vs The State Of Bihar on 1 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157360348/
1 2. This application has been filed for quashing the order dated 27.04.203 , passed by the learned Additional District Judge - III , Rohtas, at Sasaram, in Sessions Trial No. 402 of Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.43838 of 2023(4) dt.01-04-2024 2022 , Gr. No. 309 of 2013 arising out of Dehri Town P . S. Case No. 163 of 2013 , by which the discharge petition filed by the petitioners u/s 227 Cr.
P . C has been rejected on erroneous and unsubstantiated grounds. 
3 . One Santosh Kumar, S/o Surye Dev Yadav, alleged in his fardbayan dated March 24, 2013,
recorded by S.l. Vinod Kr. Dehri Town P.S., at 9.35 AM at Bose Clinic, Dehri, that on March 23,
2013, his neighbor Santosh Kumar, S/o Nanhaku Ram, had brought a gas cylinder from the R.D.
Indane gas agency, from which gas was leaking, and a complaint in this regard had been made to the Gas Agency, but the agency did not pay any attention. The leaking gas cylinder was taken out of the house and put upside down in the drain outside the house. However, the gas leak did not stop and enveloped the vessel. At some distance, a neighbor of Santosh was cooking food. Soon the gas caught fire and spread everywhere, leading to burn injuries to 18 people. He further stated that the proprietor and staff of R.D. Gas Agency were responsible for the gas leak leading to its occurrence. 
On the basis of the said fardbayan, Dehri Town P.S. Case no. 163 of 2013, dated March 24, 2013,
came to be registered under Section 285, 286, 308, and 120 B IPC against the proprietor and staff of R.D. Indonesian Gas Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.43838 of 2023(4) dt.01-04-2024 Agency. 
4. Petitioner No. 1 is proprietor of the R. D. Indane Gas Agency , petitioner No. 2 is father-in-law of petitioner No. 1 and petitioner No. 3 is staff of the said agency . 
5 . It is submitted on behalf of the petitioners that they are innocent and have been falsely implicated in the present case. During the investigation, it was revealed that the said Santosh Kumar, S/o Nanhaku Ram, had not been delivered any gas cylinders by the R.D. Indane gas agency on March 23, 2013. Rather, a gas cylinder had been provided to him on 21/2/2013 by the agency,
and he had booked a fresh delivery on 22/3/2013, but no delivery had been made till the date of the fire accident. It was further stated that, as per the statement of the said Santosh Kumar u/s 161 Cr.P.C., he himself had fitted a pressure regulator (PR) on the cylinder valve on March 24, 2013, as no one other than himself had the idea of fixing the PR and he had been out of Dehri for the last two days. After fising, he checked if it was working and found that after keeping PR in the off position,
the burner was still on. When he put off PR from the cylinder, he felt leakage of LPG from the valve,
and leakage was increasing with a whistle-type sound. He then lifted the cylinder and put it on the gully in front of the house (without Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.43838 of 2023(4)
dt.01-04-2024 putting a safety cap on the valve). As per Santosh Kumar, he did not get time to call the R.D. Indian Gas agency. As for Santosh Kumar, it was hardly a few minutes of a leaking cylinder on the road; a spark, either from some neighbors or from the electricity, led to the accident. The investigating officer, vide a letter dated December 15, 2014, addressed to the Chief Area Manager,
Indian Oil Corporation Limited, Patna Area Office, made an inquiry with regard to the seized cylinder, whether the same had expired, the reasons for the leakage, the agency that had delivered the gas cylinder, etc. In reply to the above inquiry, the Chief Area Manager, vide his letter dated February 3, 2015, gave a detailed report, as per which the valve pin stuck due to foreign particles,
which pressed the pin downward and remained in the same position. When the gas was leaking, no one put a safety cap on it to stop the leakage. As the leakage increased, LPG was sprayed over a wide Ruchi Singh vs The State Of Bihar on 1 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157360348/
2 area, and a backfire towards the cylinder took place. From the physical examination of the cylinder at police custody, it was evident that the valve and o- ring were not damaged, and the pin was stuck at that time. Therefore, after engaging the regulator with the cylinder, the foreign particle may have stuck. Again, in a letter dated May 11, 2015, the Chief Area Manager of Indian Oil Corporation Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.43838 of 2023(4) dt.01-04-2024 Limited, Patna Area Office, informed the police that no delivery43838 had been made for the booking done on March 22, 2013. The LPG accident occurred on March 24, 2013. It was therefore confirmed that the delivery of the said cylinder had not been made by M/s R. D. Taking into consideration the reports as well as other facts that came into light during the investigation, the Sub Divisional Police officer directed the investigating officer to submit the final report on the ground of "lack of evidence." However, the Superintendent of Police, Rohtas, did not agree with the supervision report of the sub-divisional police officer and directed the I.O. to submit a charge sheet against Ruchi Singh, ( the proprietor ),
Ambika Singh, ( Supervisor ), Lalan Paswan, ( storekeeper ), and Md. Ibrahim, ( technician), 
whereupon Charge-sheet No. 520/2016, dated December 31, 2016, was filed against these persons under secs. 285, 304, 308, and 34 IPC. Thereafter, vide order dated June 13, 2018, the learned SDJM, Dehri, took cognizance of the offenses under secs. 285, 304, 308, and 34 IPC against three persons, namely:
Ruchi Singh, Ambika Singh and Lalan Paswan ( Store Keeper ). The case was committed to the Court of the 3rd Additional District Judge by order dated August 18, 2022. After the commitment of the case, before the hearing on the point of Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.43838 of 2023(4) dt.01-04-2024 charge, the petitioners filed a discharge petition dated March 2, 2023, on the ground that there was no conclusive proof that the leaking gas cylinder had been delivered by the R.D. Indane Gas agency; rather, as per the report of the Chief Area Manager, Indian Oil Corporation Limited, Patna Area Office, the alleged gas cylinder had not been supplied by the R.D. Indane Gas agency. In case of leakage, the safety cap supplied with the cylinder should have been immediately fixed, which was not done by Santosh Kumar. The investigation clearly revealed that the leaking gas cylinder was kept in the drain upside down without fixing the safety cap, as a result of which the gas spread over the entire area. Purely due to the negligence of the said Santosh Kumar, S/o Nanhaku Ram, the unfortunate accident took place, for which he alone is responsible. The statement of the informant was in contradiction to the statement given by Santosh Kumar, S/o Nanhaku Ram, who clearly stated that on March 24,
2013, at 8:00 AM, he opened the gas cylinder, fixed the regulator, and found leakage from the cylinder. He thereafter took out the cylinder from his house and kept it in the drain outside the house. He further stated that there was chulha burning near his house, and while electricity came, there was a spark, which led to the fire accident. 
The last supply of LPG Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.43838 of 2023(4)
dt.01-04-2024 cylinders to Santosh Kumar, S/o Nanhaku Ram, was made on February 23, 2013, i.e., one month prior to the incident, and thereafter, no supply of gas cylinders was made to him by the R.D. Indonese Gas Agency. During the search of the house of Santosh Kumar, S/o Nanhaku Ram, after the fire accident, a second gas cylinder was found in his house, whereas the said Santosh Kumar was the Ruchi Singh vs The State Of Bihar on 1 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157360348/ 
3 consumer of only one gas cylinder. Though the LPG distribution ship stood in the name of Ruchi Singh, she stays with her husband in Chandigarh and has nothing to do with the day-to-day work of the gas agency. Similarly, Ambika Prasad Singh is a retired engineer and the father-in-law of Ruchi Singh. He has nothing to do with the workings of the gas agency. Ambika Prasad Singh and Lalan Paswan are not named in the FIR, and without any substantial evidence, only with an ulterior motive, they have been implicated in this case. Lalan Paswan is the storekeeper of the gas agency,
whose duty it is only to store the gas cylinders. As such, no offence is made out against these petitioners, and the present application is fit to be quashed. 
6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the opposite party opposed the arguments advanced on behalf of the petitioners and submitted that due to the leakage of the cylinder, Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.43838 of 2023(4) dt.01-04-2024 some persons became injured due to the spread of fire;
eighteen persons sustained injuries, out of which ten died. It is also apparent from the record that,
after the completion of the investigation, a charge sheet has been submitted against the owner,
operator, storekeeper, etc. of the offending gas agency. He next submits that there are sufficient materials on record against these petitioners, and it cannot be said that prima facie no case is made against these petitioners. Hence, no interference is required by this court at this stage . 
7. From bare perusal of the FIR, it is apparent that the informant was not aware whether the cylinder in question was supplied by the agency or not, and he came to know about this fact only through his neighbor Santosh Kumar. During the course of the investigation, it has also come in light that the cylinder in question was not delivered by the aforementioned agency or its staff. 
Continuation of proceedings against these petitioners would amount to abuse of the process of the court. 
8 . In view of the foregoing discussions, order dated 27.04.203 , passed by the learned Additional District Judge - III , Rohtas, at Sasaram, in Sessions Trial No. 402 of 2022 , Gr. No. 309 of 2013 arising out of Dehri Town P . S. Case No. 163 of 2013 is hereby quashed with respect to these petitioners. Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.43838 of 2023(4) dt.01-04-2024 9. Accordingly, the present quashing application is allowed. 
(Prabhat Kumar Singh, J) Koushik/-

During the course of the investigation, it has also come in light that the cylinder in question was not delivered by the aforementioned agency or its staff.

Continuation of proceedings against these petitioners would amount to abuse of the process of the court.
summary.decision:
8 . In view of the foregoing discussions, order dated 27.04.203 , passed by the learned Additional District Judge - III , Rohtas, at Sasaram, in Sessions Trial No. 402 of 2022 , Gr. No. 309 of 2013 arising out of Dehri Town P . S. Case No. 163 of 2013 is hereby quashed with respect to these petitioners.
Accordingly, the present quashing application is allowed.
